verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents an official MCP server and CLI for managing flags, plus scopable API tokens, so an agent can create and toggle flags. It also has an Approvals feature. However, the evidence frames approval as something a member has "the option to request". Nothing shows the platform can require approval for agent, API, or MCP writes to production. Token scoping restricts which operations a token can perform, but it is not an approval workflow. missing for 10: evidence that approvals can be made mandatory per environment, evidence that approval gates apply to API/CLI/MCP-originated changes, explicit flag create/toggle endpoints in the evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can create and toggle flags through documented APIs, CLIs, or MCP — and the platform can force my changes through approval workflows instead of letting me write to production unreviewed

citations.quote: you enable the server, then use it to manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language.
set up and manage your feature flags, account members, projects, environments, teams, and other resources directly from the command line.
You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform.
they have the option to request approval for that change from a member or team in their LaunchDarkly project.
